entities.name: Paul de Thermes
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Paul de La Barthe de Thermes (1482–1562), a distinguished Maréchal of France, embodied the martial spirit and strategic acumen required by the French monarchy during the tumultuous mid-16th century, a period defined by the waning Italian Wars and the escalating rivalry with the Habsburg Empire. Born into the Gascon nobility, de Thermes rose through the ranks through a career spanning several decades, demonstrating exceptional leadership and tactical prowess across diverse European theaters, from Scotland to Piedmont. His military career culminated in the historic recapture of Calais in 1558, a pivotal event that irrevocably altered the geopolitical landscape of Western Europe by expelling the last English territorial foothold on the French mainland after 211 years.

De Thermes’s extensive military career saw him participate in numerous significant campaigns. As Lieutenant-General of the French forces in Scotland from 1549 to 1550, he played a crucial role in the 'Rough Wooing,' defending Scottish sovereignty against English incursions and strengthening the Auld Alliance. He achieved notable success at the Battle of Renty in 1554, where his forces decisively contributed to a French victory over Emperor Charles V's imperial army, securing French positions in Picardy. Later, as Governor of Calais following its capture, he oversaw its integration into the French crown, managing its defenses and administration until his death. His strategic planning and execution, particularly during the swift and unexpected siege of Calais, showcased an innovative approach to early modern siegecraft and combined arms tactics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Paul de Thermes's command of the French forces that recaptured Calais in 1558 definitively ended over two centuries of English territorial presence in France, a monumental achievement that reshaped Anglo-French relations and solidified French national identity. His actions directly contributed to consolidating the French monarchy's power.
